transcript.content: Hello. I'm glad you're here today. What brings you in to see me?

I'm here because I have an intense, overwhelming fear of dogs that I've been struggling with for almost two years now. It's been going on for about a year and eleven months, and it has just gotten too difficult for me to manage on my own. I'm really hoping to get some help with it.
Did this intense fear of dogs start after a specific scary or traumatic event, like being attacked or bitten by a dog?
No, I don't recall any specific scary event or dog bite that triggered this fear. It just seems to have developed on its own and has been there for about a year and eleven months now.
Do you find yourself worrying excessively about a lot of other everyday things, like your health, family, or work, or is your anxiety mostly limited to dogs?
No, I don't really worry much about everyday things like my health, family, or work. My anxiety is completely and intensely focused just on dogs.

latest_inference.note: Previously, the candidates were Specific Phobia and Generalized Anxiety Disorder. The patient has confirmed that their anxiety is entirely focused on dogs and that they do not experience excessive worry about other everyday life domains (health, family, work), which rules out Generalized Anxiety Disorder. Therefore, only Specific Phobia remains, and we can conclude the assessment.
